seoTitle: How to Delete or Hide a Conversation on Slack
metaDescription: Delete individual Slack messages, hide a direct message thread from your sidebar, or archive a channel to keep your workspace tidy.
intro: Slack doesn't give you a single button that wipes a conversation off the face of the earth for both sides — and for direct messages, that's by design, since the other person's copy of the history is theirs to keep. What you do have full control over is your own message content and your own sidebar view: you can permanently delete anything you personally posted, hide a DM thread so it stops cluttering your list, and archive a channel to freeze it in place. This guide separates those three very different actions so you pick the right one instead of assuming a DM you've hidden is actually gone.

steps.heading: Understand what 'delete' actually removes
steps.body: Deleting only ever applies to content you personally posted — a message, a file, a formatted block — unless you're a workspace admin with permission to remove other people's content. It's a permanent action for regular members: once confirmed, there's no built-in undo, and the message disappears from the conversation for everyone who can see that channel or DM, not just from your own view. This is the tool for fixing a mistake or pulling something sensitive, not for clearing an entire conversation's history.

steps.heading: Delete an individual message
steps.body: Hover over the message you want to remove until the hidden action icons appear along its right edge, then click the three-dot 'More actions' menu and choose Delete message. Slack shows a confirmation warning before it commits, because this step can't be walked back afterward. Do this for one message at a time — there's no native bulk-delete across an entire conversation in the standard interface, so clearing a long thread this way is a message-by-message process.

steps.heading: Hide a direct message from your sidebar
steps.body: If your goal is really just decluttering your own view rather than erasing anything, hovering over a DM entry in the left sidebar reveals a close (X) icon — click it and the thread disappears from your list. This does not delete a single message on either side; it only removes the sidebar shortcut for you. The conversation reappears automatically the moment that contact sends you a new message, so treat this as tidying, not deletion.

steps.heading: Archive a channel instead of a DM
steps.body: Channels work differently from direct messages because they're shared team spaces, not two-person threads. Open the channel, click its name at the top to open the details panel, and look for an Archive option (channel admins and, depending on workspace settings, regular members can do this). Archiving freezes the channel — no new messages can be posted — but keeps its full history searchable and viewable rather than deleting it outright, which makes it the safer choice when a project wraps up and you just don't want the channel cluttering the active list anymore.

steps.heading: Set a workspace-wide retention policy
steps.body: For ongoing cleanup rather than one-off deletions, workspace admins can configure message retention under workspace settings — for example, automatically clearing messages older than 30, 60, or 90 days across specific channels or the whole workspace. This is the tool for keeping storage and search results lightweight over time without anyone manually deleting anything, and it applies uniformly rather than depending on individual members remembering to clean up after themselves. Retention settings usually sit under a dedicated Data & Message Retention or similar section, and changing them workspace-wide typically requires admin or owner access.

faq.question: Can I delete a message someone else sent?
faq.answer: Only workspace admins can delete other members' messages; regular users can only delete messages they personally posted.

faq.question: Does hiding a DM delete the conversation history?
faq.answer: No, hiding just removes the thread from your sidebar view; the full history reappears if that contact messages you again.

faq.question: Is there a time limit for deleting a message?
faq.answer: Slack generally lets you delete your own messages at any time, though some workspaces set policies that restrict this window.

faq.question: Can I recover a deleted message?
faq.answer: Deleted messages typically cannot be recovered by regular users once removed — there's no built-in undo after you confirm the deletion.

faq.question: What's the difference between archiving a channel and deleting messages in it?
faq.answer: Archiving freezes a channel so no new activity can be posted, but its full history stays intact and searchable. Deleting a message removes that specific content permanently.
